conf.description: printers-mfd scan-send-jobs dataset, syslog-kv format (HP FutureSmart branch): hand-built header+kv decode of HP job-completion messages, split off the same syslog grammar as the device-security-syslog HP branch but a distinct event family; no stock integration or pack exists.

conf.comment: printers-mfd / scan-send-jobs / syslog-kv: HP job-completion messages, same header+kv grammar as the device-security-syslog HP branch ('<priority> <device type>: <event summary>; key=value pairs') but a different event family (scan/copy/fax/print job completion vs security/config events); built as its own pipeline per the one-pipeline-per-dataset-and-format rule even though a real deployment could share one pipeline branching on event family. device_type is parsed but dropped -- this dataset's field table does not target observer.type. This feed is genuinely thin: scan-to-* messages carry no filename, recipient, or byte count, so recipient-level attribution is out of scope by design, not an implementation gap. job_type's vendor-documented misspelling 'reveived_fax' is normalized to 'received_fax'; source_IP's literal 0.0.0.0 on device-generated reports is nulled rather than indexed as a real source per the map's own instruction.

functions.description: record the thin-feed scope, the job_type typo normalization, and the 0.0.0.0 source_IP drop
split the syslog PRI, device type, free-text event summary, and the trailing key=value block
extract the key=value pairs (job_name, job_type, destination_type, destination, drive_name, user, source_IP, hostname, outcome, time)
decompose HP's 12-hour 'YYYY-MMM-DD HH:MM AM/PM (UTC+HH:MM)' device time into components for RFC3339 reconstruction
batch-rename the straight-copy status:mapped/partial fields to their ECS targets

invert the RFC5424 severity derived from PRI into event.severity, normalize job_type's documented misspelling, split user's REALM\user prefix, null out the literal 0.0.0.0 source_IP, fold event.outcome, route the unmapped kv fields to mfd.job.*, and build an ISO-8601 string from the decomposed device time
set Cribl's canonical event time from the reconstructed RFC3339 device time (never write @timestamp directly)
drop the temp ISO-string field and tag the event with its dataset (no hyphens, per the Elastic data-stream naming constraint)
